_comment: Synthetic CloudTrail fixture modeled on an AWS MCP Server OAuth session (agent traffic). All identifiers are fictitious.
_notes: Correlation key is aws:SignInSessionArn (session/00000000-...). It appears in additionalEventData on the CreateOAuth2Token grant, and in userIdentity.sessionContext on every subsequent event made under the OAuth token.

CreateOAuth2Token: requestParameters.resource is the AWS MCP Server; userAgent is the MCP client (Bun); grant_type=authorization_code. This is the distinguishing marker of an MCP OAuth grant vs. aws login (see aws_login_session.json).

ListUsers (iam.amazonaws.com): the modeled AWS API call. userAgent AND sourceIPAddress are 'aws-mcp.amazonaws.com', and userIdentity.invokedBy is 'aws-mcp.amazonaws.com' — the AWS MCP Server made the call on the user's behalf. sessionContext.signInSessionArn ties it to the grant.

CallReadWriteTool (aws-mcp.amazonaws.com): a new eventType 'AwsMcpEvent' recording the MCP tool invocation itself. userAgent identifies a representative agent client. additionalEventData.downstreamRequests links the tool call to the iam:ListUsers API call it triggered.
trailtool tags the resulting session SessionType 'agent' by matching sessionContext.signInSessionArn to the MCP CreateOAuth2Token grant.
Account, identity, credential, IP, and session values are synthetic and safe to publish.

Records._comment: Step 1: AWS Sign-In mints the OAuth access token for the AWS MCP Server. signInSessionArn (in additionalEventData) is the correlation key. No AuthorizeOAuth2Access is required when reusing an active browser sign-in session.

Step 2: The agent's tool invocation, recorded by the AWS MCP Server as an AwsMcpEvent. userAgent identifies a representative client. downstreamRequests links to the iam:ListUsers call it triggered. sessionContext.signInSessionArn matches the grant.

Step 3: The AWS API call the MCP Server made on the user's behalf. userAgent and sourceIPAddress are aws-mcp.amazonaws.com, invokedBy is aws-mcp.amazonaws.com, and sessionContext.signInSessionArn matches the grant — this is what marks it as agent traffic.
